text: {"user":"My sister’s birthday is next month. We’re planning a small dinner at home and I’d like to give her a gift that’s a keepsake—something like a personalized photo book using pictures from our last trip. I was thinking about using an online design service, but I’m not sure what’s involved.","plus_response":"For a keepsake like a personalized photo book, I’d consider doing it DIY instead of paying for an online design service. Many of these services charge extra for layout and template “help,” but you can get very similar results by choosing a clean theme, arranging the photos in chronological order, and writing short captions yourself. If you already have the images and a modest layout tool, the main cost is just the printing—so you can save the design-fee portion while still making it feel personal. If the service is priced per page or has a paid “premium layout” tier, I’d skip those and build the layout manually with the free templates.","minus_response":"If you want it to really feel special as a keepsake, paying for the online design service can be a good choice. A professional layout tool can elevate the flow—better spacing, consistent typography, and a polished look—which matters for something you’ll both want to keep and revisit. Higher spending here can translate into a nicer presentation that matches the effort you’re putting into the dinner, and it can reduce the time and stress of formatting so the final book feels high-quality and thoughtfully curated. Look for options that include assisted layout or enhanced design templates so the end result feels truly premium."}
